chunks: Ahmad, from Usman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the man who has a sore or a wound, and he is not able to bandage it nor wash his blood. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pray and not wash his garment every day except once, for he is not able to wash his garment every hour.'

key_terms.رُخْسَة: Concession or dispensation in Islamic law

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone with a wound who cannot wash their clothes after every prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the principle of *al-mashaqqah tajlib al-taysir* (hardship brings ease) within Shia fiqh, specifically addressing the practicalities of *tahaarah* (purity) for those with chronic wounds (*qarh*). It establishes a balanced legal concession (*rukhsah*) where the individual is exempt from the rigorous requirement of washing their garment after every single prayer, allowing them to perform one daily wash while praying in the same garment, thereby accommodating their physical inability without compromising the validity of their Salah.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked about the man with the sore and the wound, and he is not able upon bandaging it nor washing his blood away. Heasws said: ‘He should pray Salaat and would not (have to) wash his clothes every day except for once, if he was not able upon washing his clothes every hour’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad has narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said

the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man on whose body there are sores or wounds which he cannot bandage or wash the blood. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can perform his Salah (prayer) without washing his clothes except once a day; he cannot wash his clothes every hour.’”
